solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Suffer Bible classes with a holy man (2,6)

blocks.note: to stand something is to suffer it, as in 'I can't stand it'
RE = Religious Education, the school subject
w = with, as in w/

annotation.surface: Someone groans through Sunday school lessons alongside a clergyman.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is 'a holy man', so 'with' has to do double duty: it supplies W and also sits just before the definition. St Andrew is the apostle and patron saint of Scotland.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: apostles and saints are the holy men of the church calendar, and Andrew is both.

entries.clue: East African, hence from Timbuktu? (8)

blocks.note: so = hence, therefore
Timbuktu is a city in Mali, so someone from there is Malian; the ? flags the example

annotation.surface: A puzzled question about whether someone from Timbuktu counts as East African.
annotation.walkthrough: Timbuktu is in West Africa, so the surface seems to be getting its geography wrong; the two halves of Africa are actually doing separate jobs.
annotation.definitionFit: Somalia is in the Horn of East Africa, so a Somalian is an East African.

entries.clue: Appropriate hour to leave town on the A59 (8)

indicators.note: the hour's letter departs from the town's name

blocks.note: Harrogate is a spa town in North Yorkshire on the A59 road
h = hour; it is removed from the front of the town

annotation.surface: A traffic instruction about the right time to get out of a town on a main road.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as an adjective (suitable hour) but is the verb: to arrogate is to appropriate, take without right. The A59 is a road in northern England.
annotation.definitionFit: To arrogate something is to claim or seize it without justification, i.e. to appropriate it.

entries.clue: Conscript’s simple clothing beginning to rub (5)

indicators.note: DAFT dresses, i.e. wraps around, the R
take only the first letter of 'rub'

blocks.note: daft = simple, foolish
first letter of rub, placed inside D…AFT

annotation.surface: A soldier's plain uniform starts to chafe.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's in 'Conscript's' stands for 'is': the conscript is the rest. 'Clothing' looks like a noun (simple clothing) but acts as a verb, one word wrapping another. To draft is to conscript, chiefly in American usage.
annotation.definitionFit: To draft someone is to conscript them into military service.

entries.clue: Girl’s unhealthy love of treacle? (7,7)

blocks.note: complex can mean a tangle, so a 'complex' of TREACLE is its letters mixed up: they spell a girl's name from Greek myth
the psychological term for a daughter's fixation on her father

annotation.surface: A girl with a worrying craving for treacle, the British name for golden syrup or molasses.
annotation.walkthrough: ELECTRA is an anagram of TREACLE, so the Electra complex is literally a complex (a mix-up) of treacle. The surface suggests a sweet tooth; the question mark admits the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: The Electra complex is the Freudian-style term for a girl's excessive attachment to her father.

entries.clue: Last staunch supporter (4)

blocks.note: a verb here: endure, remain, keep going
a brace or prop, like the ropes that hold a ship's mast upright

annotation.surface: The one loyal backer who remains at the end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective describing the supporter, but it is the verb: to stay the course is to last. A stay is also a supporting rope or strut.
annotation.definitionFit: To stay is to last or endure; a stay is also a firm support.

entries.clue: Time on vehicle heading off boredom (6)

indicators.note: the head, i.e. first letter, of the word goes

blocks.note: t = time
a medium is a vehicle for conveying something; lose its first letter M

annotation.surface: Spending time on a car journey with nothing to do.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle' suggests a car, but here it is the abstract sense: a medium or means of expression.
annotation.definitionFit: Tedium is boredom, the state of being weary of dull things.

entries.clue: Landowner from the old country (6)

blocks.note: ye = the in old spelling, as in 'Ye Olde Tea Shoppe'
Oman, the Gulf state

annotation.surface: A landed gentleman who hails from his ancestral homeland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The old country' reads as one phrase meaning homeland; it has to be split so 'the old' gives YE.
annotation.definitionFit: A yeoman was a man who owned and farmed a small estate of his own land.

entries.clue: How Soviet radar misused a broadcast method (9,5)

indicators.note: the letters are used wrongly, i.e. rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

annotation.surface: A Cold War question about the Russians abusing their radar to transmit.
annotation.walkthrough: The Cold War surface fits well: shortwave radio was how stations like Radio Moscow broadcast abroad.
annotation.definitionFit: Shortwave radio carries broadcasts over long distances, so it is a method of broadcasting.

entries.clue: Canterbury pilgrim open to love on the way north (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means read upwards, i.e. backwards

blocks.note: frank = open, candid
love = nil, zero in tennis scoring; reversed to LIN

annotation.surface: A pilgrim with an open heart, travelling north to Canterbury.
annotation.walkthrough: The Franklin is one of the storytellers in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales. Canterbury is in fact south-east of most of England, so 'on the way north' is only a direction for the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The Franklin, a landowning gentleman, is one of Chaucer's pilgrims to Canterbury.

entries.clue: Search through swamp for an African city (9)

indicators.note: RAKE goes through the middle of MARSH

blocks.note: marsh = swamp; it surrounds the search
to rake through is to search thoroughly

annotation.surface: Wading through a swamp in search of a lost African city.
annotation.walkthrough: Marrakesh is a city in Morocco.
annotation.definitionFit: Marrakesh is a major city in Morocco, North Africa.

entries.clue: What Lady Godiva did with nothing on show (5)

blocks.note: Lady Godiva famously rode naked through Coventry
O = nothing, zero

annotation.surface: Lady Godiva riding naked through the streets as a public spectacle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With nothing on' is the Godiva legend itself, so it is hard to split 'on' off as the link to the definition 'show'.
annotation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a show of riding skills, especially with broncos and cattle.

entries.clue: Run on the level (5)

blocks.note: British slang for running off, using your legs
honest, above board; short for legitimate

annotation.surface: Running along flat ground.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the level' looks like flat ground but means honest, which is what legit means; 'leg it' is British slang for running off.
annotation.definitionFit: Legit, short for legitimate, means genuine or above board: on the level.

entries.clue: One’s escaped from a naturalist worryingly? (9)

definitions.text: One’s escaped from a naturalist worryingly?

indicators.note: the letters of 'One's' leave the phrase
the rest is worried, i.e. disturbed, into a new order

blocks.note: the starting letters
one = I, plus the S of 's; both are removed, leaving ANATURALT

annotation.surface: A dangerous specimen has got loose from a nature collector's keeping.
annotation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the answer: a tarantula on the loose from a naturalist's collection is worrying. That double reading is why the question mark is there.
annotation.definitionFit: A tarantula is exactly the kind of creature whose escape from a naturalist would be alarming.

entries.clue: Source of water in Wales later abandoned (8,4)

indicators.note: wild, unrestrained, so the letters run riot

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A water supply in Wales that was later given up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' reads as left behind, the fate of an old well; here it means wild, as in dancing with abandon.
annotation.definitionFit: An artesian well taps groundwater that rises under its own pressure, a source of water.

entries.clue: Words composed to understand one’s life (8)

blocks.note: a grammatical unit: words put together with a subject and verb
'life' in prison terms is the longest term a court can hand down

annotation.surface: Writing words down to make sense of one's existence.
annotation.walkthrough: 'He got life' means a life sentence. 'To understand' tells the solver to read the second phrase that way.
annotation.definitionFit: A sentence is a set of words composed together, and also a prison term such as a life.

entries.clue: Mass slaughter Macbeth worked to cover over (8)

indicators.note: the letters of Macbeth are worked into a new shape
the rearranged letters go over the O

blocks.note: anagram fodder
o = over, the cricket abbreviation; covered by the anagram

annotation.surface: Macbeth labouring to hide a massacre he committed.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: Macbeth does try to cover up his killings. A hecatomb was originally a sacrifice of a hundred oxen.
annotation.definitionFit: A hecatomb is a great slaughter, originally a sacrifice of many animals.

entries.clue: Cycling shoes: 19 perhaps (8)

indicators.note: the letters go round, the last moving to the front

blocks.note: trainers = sports shoes; move the final S to the front

annotation.surface: Kit for a bike ride: the right shoes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycling shoes' looks like footwear for a bike; 'cycling' is the instruction. 19 down is RIDDLE, and a riddle is a coarse sieve, one kind of strainer.
annotation.definitionFit: A riddle is a large sieve for soil or gravel, so it is an example of a strainer.

entries.clue: Where nuns live without means is regularly unsuitable (12)

indicators.note: without = outside, so IN CONVENT goes around
at regular intervals, so the letters are picked at even spacing: every second one

blocks.note: nuns live in a convent
the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of MEANS IS, placed inside IN CONV…ENT

annotation.surface: A nunnery where the residents have no money is not a fit place.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking means, but it is the old sense 'outside'.
annotation.definitionFit: Inconvenient means unsuitable, awkward for someone's needs.

entries.clue: Puzzle filled throughout, almost (6)

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: permeated everywhere, as a wall full of bullet holes; the final D goes

annotation.surface: A crossword that is nearly complete.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Riddled' means filled throughout, as with holes or errors; 'almost' drops its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a question posed to baffle is the original kind of puzzle.

entries.clue: What a bedmate did has no redeeming features (6)

indicators.note: the phrase features, i.e. contains, the answer

blocks.note: haS NO REDeeming

annotation.surface: A complaint about a partner who kept one awake: there is nothing good to say about them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Features' looks like part of 'redeeming features'; it is the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Snoring is the classic thing a bedmate does that keeps the other awake.

entries.clue: Look around private houses as landlord (9)

indicators.note: to go around is to turn back on oneself, so the word is read backwards
INNER houses, i.e. contains, the reversed word

blocks.note: inner = private, as in inner thoughts
peek = look, turned round to KEEP; it goes inside INN…ER

annotation.surface: Snooping round someone's private home in the guise of the landlord.
annotation.walkthrough: The landlord here is a pub landlord, the British term for someone who runs a pub or inn.
annotation.definitionFit: An innkeeper runs an inn; in Britain a publican is called the landlord.

entries.clue: Shot in front of a theatre (5)

indicators.note: placed before, so the first piece stands ahead of the A in the answer

blocks.note: a dram is a small shot of spirits, especially whisky
as written

annotation.surface: A shooting outside a playhouse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests gunfire; it is a measure of whisky.
annotation.definitionFit: Theatre, as an art form, means drama.

entries.clue: Lament taking up online crossword? (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: e- = electronic, online, as in e-mail
a crossword is a grid

annotation.surface: Grumbling about having started doing the crossword on the internet.
annotation.walkthrough: The ? marks the playful 'e-grid' for an online crossword. The whole E-GRID is reversed, not just GRID.
annotation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song, a lament for the dead.

entries.clue: A physicist’s number plate, maybe from the rear (5)

indicators.note: read backwards, from the end

blocks.note: a number plate is a car ID; 'maybe' flags the example

annotation.surface: Spotting a scientist's registration plate on the back of a car.
annotation.walkthrough: Paul Dirac was the British physicist who predicted antimatter. 'From the rear' fits a number plate seen from behind.
annotation.definitionFit: Paul Dirac was a Nobel-winning British theoretical physicist.

entries.clue: Quilt colour that is turning blue (9)

indicators.note: RED and IE are turned round together

blocks.note: red is a colour
i.e. = id est, that is
blue = sad, down

annotation.surface: A bedspread whose colour is fading to blue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blue' sits among colour words but means low in spirits.
annotation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt, originally filled with eider duck down.

entries.clue: Stops pals taking a half-day off (4)

indicators.note: the pals take the letters away
as in 'take a day off': the letters are taken away from the word

blocks.note: pals = friends
half of FRIDAY; removed from FRIENDS

annotation.surface: Friends have their outings cut short by skiving off for an afternoon.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests time off work; 'a half-day' is literally half the word FRIDAY.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in verb form: a referee's whistle that halts a match brings it to a close.

entries.clue: A month negotiating at the front for Nato (8)

indicators.note: take the first letter of 'negotiating'

blocks.clueFragment: negotiating at the front for Nato
blocks.note: the first letter of negotiating is N, spelled out as the code word the NATO phonetic alphabet uses for it

annotation.surface: A month spent in talks at the forefront of NATO diplomacy.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about diplomacy; 'for Nato' asks for the code word NATO radio operators use for the letter N, which is November.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the NATO code word for N happens also to name the eleventh month.
